journey.title: Focus stays in the basket dialog after removing a row
journey.goal: Removing the row that holds the focused button keeps keyboard focus inside the trapped dialog

steps.title: Move to the first Remove button

functionalJourney.title: Remove a basket row with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: The basket opens, removes a row and closes

guards.title: Tab wraps inside the basket
guards.goal: Tab from the last Remove button returns to the close button

steps.title: Move backwards to the last Remove button

plan.root_cause: When a button inside the basket is activated (via Enter) and its parent list item is removed, the button loses focus because it is detached from the DOM. This causes focus to escape the trap, and the focus-trap's recovery mechanism fails because the most recently focused node is detached and cannot be refocused.
plan.repair_strategy: After removing the list item, move focus to another focusable element inside the basket (the close button) to ensure keyboard focus remains trapped.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains inside the basket dialog after removing a row, allowing continued navigation without escaping the trap.
functional_risks: Focusing the close button may announce it prematurely to screen readers, but does not alter functionality.
If the close button were hidden or disabled, focus would be lost; however, it is always present and enabled.
verification_requirements: After activating a remove button with Enter, the #count updates correctly.
After removal, focus is inside the basket (e.g., on #close or another basket element).
Tab navigation continues to cycle within the basket trap.

plan.root_cause: When a remove button is activated via keyboard (Enter), the click handler removes the parent <li> from the DOM. The button loses focus because it's detached, and the focus trap's recovery mechanism does not restore focus to another element in the basket, causing focus to escape the trap.
plan.repair_strategy: After removing the list item, explicitly move focus to the close button (which is always present and focusable) to keep focus inside the basket dialog.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains inside the basket dialog after removing a row, allowing continued navigation without escaping the trap.
functional_risks: Focusing the close button may announce it prematurely to screen readers, but does not alter functionality.
If the close button were hidden or disabled, focus would be lost; however, it is always present and enabled.
verification_requirements: After activating a remove button with Enter, the #count updates correctly.
After removal, focus is inside the basket (e.g., on #close or another basket element).
Tab navigation continues to cycle within the basket trap.
